slides.label: A HUNTER WHO ALREADY TRUSTS YOU
lines: They found you, paid you, hunted your country and slept in your camp.
A new hunter takes ads and weeks of back and forth. This one takes one honest email at the right time.

slides.label: THE WHOLE SEQUENCE
rows: WITHIN A WEEK OF THE HUNT

slides.label: EMAIL 1 · THE THANK-YOU
slides.sub: Send within a week of the hunt ending. No ask in this one.
slides.subject: Thank you from [Camp name]
body: Thanks for hunting with us. I keep coming back to [one specific moment: the bull at first light on day four, the long pack out].
I'm sorting through photos and will send you the good ones this week. Safe travels home.

slides.label: EMAIL 2 · THE REBOOK
slides.sub: Send in December or January, before they've booked elsewhere.
slides.subject: Next season at [Camp name]: dates are open
body: Dates for [year] are open. I've got [number] spots in [month range] and I'm giving past clients first pick.
A [deposit amount] deposit holds your spot. Reply here and I'll send details.
slides.note: Only say "first pick" and the spot count if they're true. Your clients will notice.

slides.label: EMAIL 3 · THE APPLICATION REMINDER
slides.sub: Spring, draw states only. Send 2–3 weeks before your state's deadline.
slides.subject: Tag deadline is [date]
body: Quick heads up: the [state] elk application deadline is [date]. [Link to the agency's page]
If you draw, I'm holding [dates] for you. If you don't, let me know and we'll figure out next year.

slides.label: THE ONE FOLLOW-UP
lines: Ten days of silence? Send one line, then stop.
"Wanted to make sure this didn't get buried. Dates are still open if you're thinking about [year]."

slides.label: FOUR MISTAKES TO AVOID
items: "Premier guided experiences" gets deleted. "That bull on day four" gets read.
The thank-you has to be a thank-you.
By then they've booked, or drawn somewhere else.
Say the number and the month.
